newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl to urge expellees to accept Czech pact - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kohl to urge expellees to accept Czech pact - paper.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl will urge ethnic Germans expelled from Czech territory after World War Two to accept a declaration intended to lay to rest wartime grievances between the countries, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

The so-called Sudeten Germans are the main obstacle to a parliamentary declaration of reconciliation intended to put the Czech Republic on the same friendly footing with Germany as the other countries which the Nazis invaded.

Kohl said in September that he wanted the text to be approved by the end of the year. The Berliner Zeitung said in an advance release from Wednesday's edition that he now planned to talk to the Sudeten Germans himself.

The Sudeten Germans, backed by the Bavarian CSU who are partners in Kohl's coalition, have demanded that Prague consult with them directly and acknowledge that the expulsion of 2.5 million ethnic Germans after the war was an injustice.

Prague argues that the expulsion was legitimate in principle, although often carried out with regrettable brutality. It wants compensation from Germany for victims of the Nazi occupation like that already accorded to other countries.
